title: Infisical

tagline.en: Open-source secrets manager for teams and infrastructure
tagline.es: Gestor de secretos de código abierto para equipos e infraestructura
tagline.fr: Gestionnaire de secrets open source pour les équipes et l'infrastructure
tagline.pt: Gerenciador de segredos de código aberto para equipes e infraestrutura
tagline.ja: チームとインフラ向けのオープンソースシークレット管理
tagline.ru: Менеджер секретов с открытым исходным кодом для команд и инфраструктуры
tagline.hi: टीमों और इन्फ्रास्ट्रक्चर के लिए ओपन-सोर्स सीक्रेट्स मैनेजर

notes: First run: open the site and sign up. The first account becomes the instance (server) administrator, so do it right after the install. Then close sign-ups in the Server Admin Console (Admin → General → Allow user signups: disabled), or restrict them to your email domain.

ENCRYPTION_KEY must be 16 bytes of hex (32 characters). It is derived in the start command from the 32-character ENCRYPTION_KEY_SEED secret with sha256sum and cut -c1-32, so a recreated container gets the same key; the seed variable is unset before Infisical starts. Never change the seed: everything stored is encrypted under it.
AUTH_SECRET is the base64 form of a 32-character secret (exactly 32 bytes), as Infisical requires; changing it signs everyone out.
Infisical runs its database migrations itself on every start, so there is no separate migration job.

PostgreSQL 16.15 (the version Infisical is tested with) and Redis 7.4.7 each have a named volume and no published port. Redis is a required, persistent store for Infisical (queues, scheduled jobs), so it runs with append-only persistence and the noeviction policy upstream asks for.
SMTP is not configured, so invitation and password-reset emails are not sent.
The healthcheck probes /api/status on 127.0.0.1:8080 with the image's wget. Redis uses the panel database-memory default, like the database.
